# .github/AGENTS.md — CI-failure runbook

Read this file when a check fails, not before.

You are editing an enforcement instrument. Read the vendored `ENFORCEMENT.md` before this lands.

## Reproduce locally

```bash
pnpm check:ci         # everything reusable-checks.yml runs: check:static plus every package's tests
pnpm check:static     # the static-checks job alone (format, lint, typecheck, type tests, attw, build)
pnpm --filter <pkg> test --shard=<i>/<n>   # one shard of a test job
```

## Standing facts

- **Each CI lane owns its turbo cache key prefix** (`turbo-<os>-<lane>-<sha>`). actions/cache keys are immutable: lanes sharing a key race, and the faster lane's partial save silently drops the slower lane's entries.
- **Test jobs are planned from recorded timings.** The `plan` job reads the newest `test-timings-<profile>` artifact from main, or from any branch when main has none, and balances packages over the fewest free `ubuntu-latest` jobs whose loads fit 5 minutes (`scripts/tools/test-timings.ts`). Each job builds first, then runs its packages' tests one at a time (`turbo run test --concurrency=1`), so its wall time is the sum it was planned from and each recorded duration is uncontended. The test run keeps the builds in its graph, never `--only`, so each test key carries every dependency's build hash; the builds are cache hits after the build step. A package over 5 minutes runs as vitest shards. The `timings` job records every measured package into this run's `test-timings-<profile>` artifact, so the next run of the same profile re-packs automatically.
- **The reusable workflows are shared with other repositories.** Consumers call them pinned by commit SHA; their contract is [Calling the reusable workflows](#calling-the-reusable-workflows). Everything specific to this repository is in the callers' inputs (`ci.yml`, `mutation.yml`, `commitlint.yml`, `nix.yml`) and in `.github/actions/checks-lane`, this repository's lane hook. To change this repository's steps, edit that action; to change the shape, edit the workflow and keep its inputs backward compatible for pinned callers.
- **A lane picks its conformance profile.** A pull request runs `reusable-checks.yml` with `profile: local`; the merge queue and pushes to main run the default `per-change`; `release.yml` gates at `per-change`. Every lane runs every test file of every package: no lane leaves a test out by its name or location (`CONST-T12`). `local` runs 25 seeds and one preemption, `per-change` keeps what each check asks for. A local run measures different durations than a per-change one, so timing records are keyed by profile (`test-timings-local` / `test-timings-per-change`) and each lane plans from its own measurements.
- **Mutation runs per project with the installed `stryker` CLI, never on a pull request.** `mutation.yml` runs nightly on main (`schedule`, 14:17 UTC, the org's quietest hour for Actions runs) and on `workflow_dispatch`, never on a push or a pull request; each run takes a concurrency group of its own run id, so no run cancels another. It calls `reusable-mutation.yml`, whose `guard` job, before anything installs and with every other job needing it, refuses a pull request, a run whose ref is not the default branch (`mutation-off-main`) and a `sha` input the default branch's tip does not hold (`mutation-sha-off-main`; `mutation-night guard`, `scripts/tools/mutation-night.ts`, runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor --` against a full-history checkout; the default branch is `github.ref_name` on a schedule). A dispatch takes `sha`, `packages` (a JSON array of package names; anything but a non-empty array of packages with a `mutation` task fails the plan with `mutation-packages-invalid`) and `night`, and every run is titled `Mutation <sha>`, with `for <night>` on a re-test. Its `plan` job installs the workspace, then `mutation-admit` (`scripts/tools/mutation-admit.ts`; the decision is `mutation-admission.ts`) judges every package with a `mutation` or `mutation:*` script: a Node probe loads, in the plan job's environment, the config Stryker would discover and the package's own `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config`, and the plan fails before any Stryker run with one `::error title=<reason>` annotation per refusal: `mutation-script` (any mutation script but `"mutation": "stryker run"`), `no-workflow-file`, `missing-mutation-script` (a workspace package outside the plan, the root excepted, that holds a file of the shared mutated set as Node's glob expands it), `hidden-workflow-file` (any package holding a file under a hidden path that the shared patterns would match: Node's glob skips it, Stryker's matcher mutates it), `shared-test-file` (the installed `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config`'s shared set holds a test file: upgrade it), `config-unloadable`, `own-mutate-targets` (any `mutate` but `sharedConfig.mutate` untouched), `non-workflow-target`, `test-file-target`, `own-ignore-patterns` (an ignore pattern beyond the shared ones as they stood before the config ran), `ignored-workflow-file` (a shared file under a directory a kept shared ignore pattern, `node_modules` or `*.tsbuildinfo` names, which Stryker's crawl drops), `scoped-mutation` (any `since`) or `own-output-paths` (a Stryker output path, every one of which the crawl ignores, set to a value other than the shared one). Then turbo decides which projects the run covers: on a schedule, the `mutation` tasks `turbo query affectedTasks` reports between the commit of the newest scheduled night whose `mutation-night-<run id>` record says green and this commit (the plan job checks out full history; the query output is in the step summary), and every package turbo lists with a `mutation` task when no green night is found or its commit is not in the history; the `mutation` task's turbo `inputs` hold the lane's workflows, tools, seed costs and Deno lockfile beside `$TURBO_DEFAULT$`, so a change to the lane selects every project; on a dispatch, the packages its `packages` input names, else every package. Beside turbo sit only the closed-list items of turbo-task-graph, each named in a comment at its site: the base-commit lookup, shard sizing and batch packing by measured cost, and Stryker's own incremental record. Per selected project: `stryker plan` sized to `target-seconds` (600 s) shards from the measured seconds per mutant in `.github/mutation-seed-costs.json` (its slowest rate for a project it does not name), or from the incremental record's per-mutant `costs` only when the record measured (`actualMs`) every mutant the plan lists (`scripts/tools/mutation-shard-plan.ts` runs the passes, pricing in `scripts/tools/record-pricing.ts`): stryker leaves CompileError, Ignored, NoCoverage and new mutants unmeasured and prices them at the whole suite. The plan summary names each project's pricing source. A shard's wall estimate prices the plan's own reported predictedSeconds, so a CLI pricing change re-plans at a corrected target instead of over-packing a shard past the 60-minute backstop (both tested in `scripts/tools/mutation-shard-plan.test.ts`). The target sizes shards and never stops one: the plan summary reports each project's costliest shard and warns, naming the project and its cost source, when one is predicted over the target. Every mutation job's one time limit is `timeout-minutes: 60`, Stryker's dry run gets the same 60 minutes from `sharedConfig`, and each job writes its wall time and status to its step summary. A job killed at that limit concludes `cancelled` with GitHub's own annotation ("The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 60m0s"); the `report` job then names it with a `mutation-job-cancelled` annotation, every failure summary names its job by matrix slug and shard (`shard-<slug>-<k>of<n>`), and the plan summary has already named that project's costliest predicted shard and warned when it was over the target. A failure summary's reproduce command for a job that runs Stryker is the lane's dispatch on main (`gh workflow run Mutation --ref <default branch> -f sha=<sha> -f packages='<the job's packages>'`) with the job-minutes the plan predicts for them, labelled "reproduce through a dispatch on main", since Stryker never runs locally; the `report` job's is the whole lane's dispatch. A scheduled run ends with a `night` job (never on a dispatch, a reproduce included): it writes the night's record as the 90-day artifact `mutation-night-<run id>` (range, verdict, conclusion, planned and reported packages, survivors and failures, candidate merges, open tasks), which says green only when the run ended `success` and every planned package reported with no survivor or failure, and then either prints one line, `<run id> <from>..<to> green`, or routes a red night: the step summary holds the full report (every candidate merge in the range — from the last green night's commit, else the previous scheduled night's — and every item), and one comment on the newest candidate merge's pull request carries it, mentioning every candidate's opener since the lane has no triage, edited in place on later nights, so a night never comments on every candidate merge; a green night closes the one open task with a single comment, and a red night whose candidate merges have no pull request fails `mutation-night-unrouted` with the summary holding the task. A night with no record (a startup failure, or the `night` job failing with `mutation-night-failed`) is caught outside the lane. Then one `coverage` dry run reused by every shard, `shard` jobs, then `merge` and `gate`; single-shard projects run in `batch` jobs. Every gate holds its project against an accepted set with no ids (`{"schemaVersion":1,"survivors":[]}`, written by the job, never committed), so any survivor fails it, as `thresholds.break: 100` does for a whole run. Only the `report` job saves the `stryker-incremental-<dir>-<run_id>` cache the next plan reads. Every job restores it into each project's `reports/stryker-incremental.json`; a shard job moves it to `reports/stryker-incremental-prior.json` first, so this run's coverage record is the shard's incremental file and the prior is read through `incrementalSources`. After each shard and batch run, `run-reuse` (`scripts/tools/run-reuse.ts`) fails the job `mutation-prior-unread` when the prior names a planned mutant yet the run found a record for none, fails a shard `mutation-coverage-unreused` when its dry-run digests differ from the coverage job's, and lists in the step summary every test the dry run flagged flaky, whose covered mutants, and every static mutant while any test is flaky, re-run on every run. A stryker config sets no `ignorePatterns` of its own (`mutation-coverage-unreused` catches it at run time in a sharded project; wrong: `ignorePatterns: []`, right: no key): shard and batch children get an `--incrementalFile` outside the project, so of the records Stryker's own exclusion list names only that copy, and the record at `reports/stryker-incremental.json`, the prior beside it and test output under `coverage/` stay out only through `sharedConfig`'s `reports` and `coverage` ignores; without it every open-closure and static mutant re-runs on every run. Source of truth: `.github/workflows/reusable-mutation.yml`.
- **Re-running failed mutation jobs reuses what already ran.** Coverage and shard artifacts carry the attempt that made them (`-a<attempt>`); each coverage guard takes the unexpired one from the newest attempt the job ran in that holds one, and a merge takes a shard's artifact only from the attempt that shard last ran in, and only when it concluded success there (`mutation-shard-failed` otherwise, naming the shard) (the merge job's download step in `reusable-mutation.yml`, untested beyond the dispatch) (`scripts/tools/job-attempt.ts`, tested by `job-attempt.test.ts`), and fails `mutation-artifact-missing`, naming the job and the attempts searched, when none does; a failed read of the run's jobs or artifacts fails `mutation-api-failed`. The report deletes coverage, shard and merged artifacts only when the run lists at least one job and every job of it (plan, coverage, shard, merge, batch) concluded success in the attempt it last ran in (a `skipped` job counts as passed); an API error, an empty job list, or any other conclusion keeps them all for a re-run of its failed jobs, and a failed cleanup only warns.
- **The merge queue is enabled in the `main` ruleset only after this shape is on main.** Every workflow that reports a required check needs the `merge_group` trigger first — `ci.yml` carries it, so the gate reports on the queue ref. Enable the queue with strict up-to-date policy off; strict would need a queue whose required checks already run on `merge_group`.
- **Never re-trigger a release by hand.** `scripts/tools/plan-release.ts` derives the phase from repository state, so a killed release leaves untagged versions the next push re-plans. Tagging and GitHub Releases are idempotent — a version whose `<pkg>@vX.Y.Z` git tag already exists is skipped (`scripts/tools/cycle.ts`, `scripts/tools/tag-released-packages.ts`).
- **There is no registry.** These packages are distributed as this repo's Nix flake outputs consumed from a git ref (pinned by `flake.lock` rev + narHash, bwrap-sandboxed), not published to npm. The release path writes a git tag and a GitHub Release per unreleased version — no npm token, no OIDC, no trusted publisher to configure.

## Calling the reusable workflows

Five workflows are callable from any repository: `reusable-checks.yml`, `reusable-mutation.yml`, `reusable-commitlint.yml`, `reusable-nix.yml` and `conflict-check.yml`. Call them pinned by commit SHA (`uses: systemfsoftware/systemfsoftware/.github/workflows/<file>@<sha>`). Every input is optional except `conflict-check`'s two; a caller writes no composite action of its own.

**Where tools and actions come from.** A reusable reaches this repository's actions through `$/.github/actions/<name>`, which resolves to the workflow's own commit, never the caller's `./`. Its Deno tools (`test-timings`, `mutation-admit`, `mutation-shard-plan`, `mutation-night`, `classify-diff`, `job-attempt`, `record-pricing`, `run-reuse`, `sfs-deps`) come from `$/.github/actions/sfs-tools`, which sparse-checks out `scripts/` at `job.workflow_repository`@`job.workflow_sha`. `$/` needs runner 2.336.0 or newer, so a self-hosted fleet must run at least that. A non-root `working-directory` checks out only that directory (except `reusable-nix.yml`, whose evaluator needs the whole tree's objects).

**Consumer prerequisites.** A pnpm workspace with a committed lockfile and a `packageManager` field. Checks: `turbo`, a `test` script per tested package, and a `build` task where one exists. Mutation: `@systemfsoftware/stryker-js` installed in the workspace root (for `stryker plan`, `run`, `merge` and `gate`) and a turbo `mutation` task; every mutated package has a `src/**/*.workflow.ts` file, a `"mutation": "stryker run"` script and no `mutation:*` variant, a `stryker.config.*` that spreads `sharedConfig` from `@systemfsoftware/stryker-config` and sets no `mutate` (`incremental: true` comes from it). A project the plan shards also needs `incrementalSources` to match `reports/stryker-incremental-*.json`, where its shard jobs hand it the previous record (`mutation-prior-unread` otherwise), and every mutated project's Stryker config must spread `sharedConfig` and set no `ignorePatterns` of its own, so `reports/` and `coverage/` stay out of Stryker's digest (`mutation-coverage-unreused` catches one that does not in a sharded project), or each run's record re-runs its unchanged mutants. Commitlint: `@commitlint/cli` and a commitlint config in the workspace root. Nix: a flake whose `packages.<system>` and `checks.<system>` are derivations.

**`.sfs-deps` tarballs (checks, mutation, commitlint).** A consumer installs systemfsoftware packages as `file:.sfs-deps/<name>-<version>.tgz` entries in `pnpm-lock.yaml`, with `.sfs-deps/` gitignored, and a flake installable in `working-directory` whose output is a directory holding exactly those `.tgz` files (`sfs-deps-installable`, default `.#sfs-deps`; `.github/consumer-fixture/flake.nix` is the pattern). Each call's `sfs-deps` job keys the tarballs on the `.sfs-deps/` paths and integrities the lockfile records (`sfs-deps-v1-<sha256>`). A warm key restores in every installing job with no Nix; a cold one installs Nix only in that job, builds the installable, checks every named tarball against its recorded integrity and saves only then. Every job that installs restores the key before the hook-or-built-in routing or its install step, so a lane hook's own install finds `.sfs-deps/` in place, and checks each restored tarball against the lockfile's integrity before anything installs it (`sfs-deps-mismatch` on a difference). A lockfile that names no `.sfs-deps/` tarball gets an empty key and no other step.

**Event policy.** On a pull request, checks and nix run only what the diff can affect: a diff inside the docs set (`docs/**`, root `*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md`, or `docs-globs`) skips build, test and nix; the plan still runs, after the classifier and without a turbo dry run, and only lanes with a `docs-run` run. The built-in `docs` phase installs, so on a docs-only diff the classifier reads the lockfile and skips the `sfs-deps` producer only when it read the lockfile and found no `.sfs-deps/` tarball; otherwise the producer runs, on the base branch's key, since a docs-only diff leaves the lockfile unchanged. Any other event, any path outside the set, or a diff that cannot be read runs everything. The test planner skips a package whose turbo hash a remote cache or a passed run already holds, and nix builds only outputs whose `drvPath` differs from the base commit's (one that fails to evaluate there builds). `reusable-mutation.yml` accepts a push, `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch` (this repository's `mutation.yml` uses only the last two): its `guard` job fails a `pull_request`, `pull_request_target` or `merge_group` event with `mutation-on-pull-request` before anything installs. Commitlint runs on pull requests only and skips Dependabot.

**Permissions the caller grants.** Checks: `contents: read`, `actions: read`. Mutation: `contents: read`, `actions: write` (merge downloads shard artifacts, the report deletes per-shard artifacts after a passing run), `pull-requests: write` (a scheduled night's `night` job comments a red night's fix task once, on the newest candidate merge's pull request). Commitlint, nix and conflict-check: `contents: read`. Checks takes the `turbo-api` and `turbo-token` secrets for a remote Turbo cache.

**The lane hook (checks only).** A caller that has `.github/actions/checks-lane/action.yml` at the root of its checkout gets it run once per phase (`plan`, a lane's id, `test`, `test-after`, `timings`, `gate`, `docs`) with inputs `lane`, `job` and `profile`; the workflow output `lane-source` is `hook`. Without one, or under a non-root `working-directory`, every phase runs `$/.github/actions/builtin-lane` and `lane-source` is `built-in`; the non-root case says so in the summary with `hook-not-visible-working-directory`. In built-in mode a `timings` of `test-timings` means this workflow's own planner, and `dry-run` defaults to `<pnpm> exec turbo run test --dry=json` on pull requests.

**On failure.** Each failing job writes one reason code, the local reproduce command and the next action to its step summary, annotates with them, and uploads its captured logs as `failure-log-<job>-<attempt>`; when a mutation project's own `stryker run` fails, that log also holds the run's full output and the child's `mutation-stream.jsonl` where one was written, which the CLI's own message only tails. The codes are a closed set (`$/.github/actions/failure-summary`): `merge-conflict`, `classify-failed`, `install-failed`, `tools-ref-missing` (sfs-tools got no workflow repository or commit, or could not fetch the tools at that commit), `plan-failed`, `hook-failed`, `lane-failed`, `build-failed`, `test-failed`, `timings-failed`, `gate-failed`, `commit-message-invalid`, `nix-eval-failed`, `nix-build-failed`, `outputs-differ-across-systems`, `compare-artifact-missing`, `mutation-on-pull-request`, `mutation-off-main`, `mutation-sha-off-main`, `mutation-packages-invalid`, `mutation-night-failed`, `mutation-night-unrouted` (a red night found no candidate merge with a pull request; the step summary holds its task), `mutation-failed`, `mutation-shard-failed`, `mutation-merge-failed`, `mutation-coverage-failed` (the newest attempt of a sharded project's coverage dry run did not pass, so its own shards and merge fail and no other project's do), `mutation-artifact-missing` (no attempt a coverage or shard job ran in left an unexpired artifact), `mutation-api-failed` (a read of the run's jobs or artifacts failed; the error names the endpoint and HTTP status), `mutation-tool-misused` (a step called `job-attempt` or `run-reuse` without readable inputs), `mutation-matrix-too-large` (the plans need more shard jobs than the 256 one GitHub matrix may create, so the plan job fails before any job runs), `mutation-shard-job-missing` (the run holds no job for a planned shard), `mutation-prior-unread` (a shard or batch run found no record for any planned mutant the prior incremental record names, or that record is not JSON), `mutation-coverage-unreused` (a shard ran its own dry run because its digests differ from the coverage job's, so a file one of them wrote under the project entered Stryker's digest), `sfs-deps-lockfile-invalid` (the lockfile is unreadable or names one tarball with two integrities), `sfs-deps-build-failed`, `sfs-deps-mismatch` (in the `sfs-deps` job, the installable lacks a named tarball or builds other bytes than the lockfile records; in an installing job, the cache entry restored under the key holds other bytes than the lockfile records), `sfs-deps-missing` (an installing job found no cache entry under the `sfs-deps` job's key, or the cache service refused the restore), `timed-out` (the job's `timeout-minutes` or a cancellation stopped a step; a summary step that runs on `failure() || cancelled()` reports it), and `unclassified` for a failure none of them names.

**This repository dogfoods them.** `ci.yml`, `mutation.yml`, `commitlint.yml` and `nix.yml` are callers, and `consumer-fixture.yml` calls `reusable-checks.yml`, `reusable-commitlint.yml`, `reusable-nix.yml` and the `mutation-event-guard` action on `.github/consumer-fixture/`, a workspace with its own lockfile, no hook and no composite, exactly as an outside repository would. It does not call `reusable-mutation.yml`: the fixture's package holds no workflow file, so it carries no mutation script, and the mutation reusable is exercised only by this repository's own dispatched runs.

### `reusable-checks.yml`

Outputs `lane-source` and `test-jobs` (the planned test jobs as JSON, each with its `packages`; `[]` when every package was skipped); secrets `turbo-api`, `turbo-token`. Inputs stay backward compatible for pinned callers: add, never rename or remove.

| Input                  | Default             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`    | `.`                 | The pnpm workspace root, relative to the repository root. A non-root value checks out only that directory and always runs the built-in lanes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `profile`              | `per-change`        | Passed to the checks-lane action unchanged; systemfsoftware's conformance profile (`local` or `per-change`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `record`               | `test-timings`      | Name of the timing record artifact the plan reads and the timings job writes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `timings`              | `test-timings`      | Command that runs the test-timings planner (the flake's `test-timings`, or a deno invocation of the script). With the built-in lanes, `test-timings` is this workflow's own planner                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `runs-on`              | `["ubuntu-latest"]` | JSON label list for the plan, timings and gate jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `test-runs-on`         | empty               | JSON label list for the test jobs and any lint lane that names none; empty means `runs-on`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `lanes`                | `[]`                | JSON list of lint lanes: {"id", "name", "timeout-minutes", "run"?, "docs-run"?, "fetch-depth"?, "runs-on"?}; `run` is a command after the lane's action. On a docs-only pull request a lane with `docs-run` runs that command after the `docs` phase instead, and a lane without one is skipped                                                                                                                                                      |
| `target`               | `300`               | Planner --target, seconds of predicted work per job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `max-jobs`             | `12`                | Planner --max-jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `max-seconds`          | `1800`              | Planner --max-seconds; keep it at or under the test job's timeout-minutes in seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `timeout-minutes`      | `30`                | Each test job's timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `plan-timeout-minutes` | `5`                 | The plan and timings jobs' timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gate-name`            | `the gate`          | Name of the job that passes only when every other job passed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `gate-lane`            | `false`             | Check out and run the checks-lane action's `gate` phase after the gate's own check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `gate-timeout-minutes` | `2`                 | The gate job's timeout                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `node-options`         | empty               | NODE_OPTIONS for the test jobs (a lint lane sets its own `node-options`); GitHub refuses it from $GITHUB_ENV                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `pnpm`                 | `pnpm`              | How the test steps invoke pnpm                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `test-flags`           | empty               | Extra flags on the packed jobs' `turbo run test`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `shard-flags`          | empty               | Extra flags on a shard job's vitest run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `persist-credentials`  | `true`              | actions/checkout persist-credentials                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `fetch-tags`           | `false`             | actions/checkout fetch-tags                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `dry-run`              | empty               | Command printing turbo's `--dry=json` for the test task without `--only` (e.g. `pnpm dlx turbo@2 run test --dry=json`), so each hash covers the task's dependencies as the test jobs' own keys do; the plan skips a package whose task is a remote cache hit, or which last passed whole on the same dry-run hash. Empty plans every package, except that the built-in lanes default it to `<pnpm> exec turbo run test --dry=json` on a pull request |
| `docs-globs`           | empty               | Newline- or comma-separated globs that replace the docs set (`docs/**`, root `*.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`, `**/CLAUDE.md`). A pull request that changes only docs skips the test and timings jobs and runs only lanes with a `docs-run`; the plan still runs                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `turbo-team`           | empty               | Remote Turbo cache team; empty leaves the remote cache off                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `sfs-deps-installable` | `.#sfs-deps`        | The flake installable that builds the lockfile's `.sfs-deps/` tarballs; see [`.sfs-deps` tarballs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### `reusable-mutation.yml`

Every job runs under `timeout-minutes: 60`, which no input changes. Removed inputs: `max-jobs`, `max-seconds`, `unknown-mutant-seconds`, `record`, `timeout-minutes` and `report-timeout-minutes`; a caller that moves its pin past their removal drops them, since GitHub refuses an input the called workflow does not declare.

| Input                  | Default                            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`    | `.`                                | The pnpm workspace root, relative to the repository root. A non-root value checks out only that directory                                                             |
| `target-seconds`       | `600`                              | Wall seconds each planned shard or batch is sized to; a shard predicted over it is reported in the plan summary and runs                                              |
| `seed-costs`           | `.github/mutation-seed-costs.json` | Measured `{projects: {<dir>: {seconds, mutants}}}` pricing a project with no incremental record; an unnamed project takes the slowest rate, a missing file 1 s/mutant |
| `runs-on`              | `["ubuntu-latest"]`                | JSON label list for every job                                                                                                                                         |
| `sfs-deps-installable` | `.#sfs-deps`                       | The flake installable that builds the lockfile's `.sfs-deps/` tarballs; see [`.sfs-deps` tarballs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows)                                   |
| `sha`                  | `""`                               | A commit on the default branch to test instead of the run's own; the guard refuses one the default branch's tip does not hold                                         |
| `packages`             | `""`                               | JSON array of package names to plan instead of every package; the plan refuses any but a non-empty array of packages with a `mutation` task                           |

### `reusable-commitlint.yml`

| Input                  | Default             | Meaning                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`    | `.`                 | The pnpm workspace root that holds the commitlint config and `@commitlint/cli`, relative to the repository root                     |
| `runs-on`              | `["ubuntu-latest"]` | JSON label list for the job                                                                                                         |
| `sfs-deps-installable` | `.#sfs-deps`        | The flake installable that builds the lockfile's `.sfs-deps/` tarballs; see [`.sfs-deps` tarballs](#calling-the-reusable-workflows) |

### `reusable-nix.yml`

| Input                    | Default                                                                                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `working-directory`      | `.`                                                                                                                  | The flake's directory, relative to the repository root                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `systems`                | `[{"system": "x86_64-linux", "runner": "ubuntu-latest"}, {"system": "aarch64-linux", "runner": "ubuntu-24.04-arm"}]` | JSON list of {"system", "runner"}: one build job per entry                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `extra-steps`            | `[]`                                                                                                                 | JSON list of {"name", "installable"?, "run"} run after the sweep, from the flake's directory; `{system}` in either string is the job's system. An entry with an `installable` (`.#<attr path>`) runs only when that derivation changed; one without always runs |
| `compare-across-systems` | empty                                                                                                                | An installable (`.#<attr path>`, `{system}` substituted) whose output every system builds on every non-docs-only run and must build byte-identical to the first system's; a system with no output fails `compare-artifact-missing`                              |
| `timeout-minutes`        | `60`                                                                                                                 | Timeout of each build job                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `docs-globs`             | empty                                                                                                                | Newline- or comma-separated globs that replace the default docs set; a pull request inside the set builds nothing                                                                                                                                               |
| `runs-on`                | `["ubuntu-latest"]`                                                                                                  | JSON label list for the classify and compare jobs                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

### `conflict-check.yml`

| Input      | Default  | Meaning                                            |
| ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `base_ref` | required | Name of the base branch the PR targets (e.g. main) |
| `head_sha` | required | SHA of the PR head commit (never the merge ref)    |

## Failure runbook

| Failure                     | Root cause                                                      | Remedy                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api:check` fails           | Public API surface changed in a package with a committed golden | `pnpm --filter <pkg> api:update` and commit `etc/*.api.md`                                            |
| Git step exits 128          | Dirty workspace cascading from a prior step                     | Inspect the first failing step, not the git step                                                      |
| Log download gives HTTP 403 | The GitHub API refuses log download without push access         | Open `https://github.com/systemfsoftware/systemfsoftware/actions/runs/<run_id>` and read the step log |
